title: Expeditionary Fuels Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
4.     MOS 1390, Expeditionary Fuels Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. The Expeditionary Fuels Officer MOS consists of technical
warrant officers who plan, coordinate, and supervise the receipt, storage,
transfer, and dispensing of bulk fuel. Frequent coordination with other
agencies, both inter-service and internationally, are required to include
direct interaction with joint petroleum offices (JPO) and the defense
logistics agency energy (DLA-E). Duties range from developing bulk fuel
sites, advising planners on fuel estimations and requirements, making
recommendations on security plans for tactical fuel systems, to emplacement
of a bulk fuel system, to writing the bulk fuel portion of operation orders.
Environmental concerns are extremely crucial in any training and operational
scenario, therefore, understanding of environmental requirements and
limitations is a must. Challenging and interesting billets include
battalions within the Marine logistics group and squadrons within the Marine
air wing, as well as instructor duty with the Marine Corps Detachment, U.S.
Army Quartermaster School, assignment as regional fuel officers, equipment
acquisition at Marine Corps Systems Command and Fuels Capabilities
Integration Officer at CD&I.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must hold MOS 1391.



                                           1-80                      Enclosure (1)
 1113                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



            (2) Must possess an MM score of 95 or higher.

        (3) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within
18 months of appointment to WO.

        (2) Complete the Petroleum Officer Course (A1431H1 (petroleum portion
of the course only)) and (A1414Z1 (USMC Bulk Fuel Officers)), U.S. Army
Quartermaster School, Ft Gregg-Adams, VA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (l), Engineer and Utilities Training and Readiness Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

        (1) First-Line supervisors/Managers of Production and Operating
Workers 51-1011.

            (2) Petroleum Pump System Operators, Refinery Operators, and Gaugers
51-8093.

        (3) First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and
Repairers 49-1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   Utilities Officer, 1120.




                                          1-81                       Enclosure (1)
 1114                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
